title: max_query_len resolves differently in compare and set_suffix_array_mem
body:
A search combines the max query length the file was built with (`SuffixSortType::MaxQueryLen(mql)`, where 0 means fully sorted) with the one the caller passes in `SearchOptions::max_query_len`. Two functions do this, and they disagree.

`SufrSearch::compare` in `libsufr/src/sufr_search.rs`:

- built `mql > 0` and caller `Some(v)`: `min(mql, v)`
- caller `Some(v)` otherwise: `v`
- caller `None`: `mql`
- a result of 0 means compare the whole query

`SufrFile::set_suffix_array_mem` in `libsufr/src/sufr_file.rs`:

- treats a built `mql` of 0 as `text_len`
- treats a caller value of 0 as "not given" and uses the built value

| built | caller | `compare` | `set_suffix_array_mem` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | `Some(0)` | 0, unbounded | 20 |
| 0 | `Some(10)` | 10 | 10 |
| 20 | `None` | 20 | 20 |

In the first row the binary search compares past position 20 in a suffix array that is only sorted to 20. The order beyond that prefix is arbitrary, so the search may return a wrong range. It is unverified whether any caller passes `Some(0)`.

Found by reading the code. Not reproduced.
